        if np.any(fast):
            qf, af, bf = q[fast], a[fast], b[fast]
            pos = af > 0
            r = np.empty(qf.shape)
            if np.any(pos):
                sa, sb = _norm_sf(af[pos]), _norm_sf(bf[pos])
                qp = qf[pos]
                r[pos] = _norm_isf(qp * sb + sa * (1.0 - qp))
            neg = ~pos
            if np.any(neg):
                na, nb = _norm_cdf(af[neg]), _norm_cdf(bf[neg])
                qn = qf[neg]
                r[neg] = _norm_ppf(qn * nb + na * (1.0 - qn))
            r = np.where(r < af, af, r)
            r = np.where(r > bf, bf, r)
            out[fast] = r
        slow = ~fast
        if np.any(slow):
            idx = np.flatnonzero(slow)
            qs, as_, bs = q.ravel(), a.ravel(), b.ravel()
            flat = out.reshape(-1)
            for i in idx:
                flat[i] = _truncnorm_ppf_scalar(qs[i], as_[i], bs[i])
        return out
"""

s=open(p).read()
old="""        out = None
        it = np.nditer([q, a, b, out], [],
                       [['readonly'], ['readonly'], ['readonly'],
                        ['writeonly', 'allocate']])
        for (_q, _a, _b, _x) in it:
            _x[...] = _truncnorm_ppf_scalar(_q, _a, _b)
        return it.operands[3]
"""
new="""        q, a, b = np.broadcast_arrays(q, a, b)
        out = np.empty(q.shape, dtype=np.result_type(q, a, b, float))
        with np.errstate(all='ignore'):
            delta = _truncnorm_get_delta(a, b)
        fast = (delta > 0) & (q > 0) & (q < 1)
        if np.any(fast):
            qf, af, bf = q[fast], a[fast], b[fast]
            pos = af > 0
            r = np.empty(qf.shape)
            if np.any(pos):
                sa, sb = _norm_sf(af[pos]), _norm_sf(bf[pos])
                qp = qf[pos]
                r[pos] = _norm_isf(qp * sb + sa * (1.0 - qp))
            neg = ~pos
            if np.any(neg):
                na, nb = _norm_cdf(af[neg]), _norm_cdf(bf[neg])
                qn = qf[neg]
                r[neg] = _norm_ppf(qn * nb + na * (1.0 - qn))
            r = np.where(r < af, af, r)
            r = np.where(r > bf, bf, r)
            out[fast] = r
        slow = ~fast
        if np.any(slow):
            idx = np.flatnonzero(slow)
            qs, as_, bs = q.ravel(), a.ravel(), b.ravel()
            flat = out.reshape(-1)
            for i in idx:
                flat[i] = _truncnorm_ppf_scalar(qs[i], as_[i], bs[i])
        return out
"""
assert old in s
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(old,new))
E

import timeit

import numpy as np
beta = np.array([-1.25,-1,-0.5])
x1 = np.random.uniform(-2,2,size=2700).reshape(900,-1); x1[:,0]=1
def w(): return truncnorm(-x1@beta, np.inf, loc=x1@beta).rvs()
print(min(timeit.repeat(w,number=1,repeat=10)))
r=w(); print(r.shape,(r>=0).all() if True else 0)
E
python /tmp/w.py; python -m pytest --no-header -q --tb=short -p no:cacheprovider scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py -k truncnorm 2>&1 | tail -5

I vectorized `truncnorm_gen._ppf` in `scipy/stats/_continuous_distns.py`, so the workload now runs in about 0.036 s per call (best of 10). I didn't time the original, so I can't state the speedup.

The old code looped over the 900 elements and called a scalar function for each one. The new code uses array operations for every element that needs the plain normal ppf/isf formula. That covers all of them in this workload. Any element that doesn't (zero-width intervals, `q` at 0 or 1, or the tail cases that need root-finding) still goes through the original scalar function.

The 15 truncnorm tests in `scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py` pass. I didn't run the rest of the test suite. I also didn't compare the new output against the old per-element results, so equivalence rests on those tests and on the new code applying the same formulas and clipping.

I timed it with a copy of the workload at `/tmp/w.py`, not the original script.
